purpose: Draft only, not registered. The orchestrator registers brawley-avra-west after its frozen run by running tools/live/verify_all_route_inlets.py, which now writes the inlet's observed object from its OBSERVED table. This file records the intended inlet config.

inlets.x: from sfincs.src / boundary-placement.json of the packaged case (filled by verify_all_route_inlets.py)
inlets.y: from sfincs.src / boundary-placement.json of the packaged case (filled by verify_all_route_inlets.py)

observedMeaning: Live runs: every hour at or before the HRRR cycle uses USGS 09487000 instantaneous discharge at the top of the hour (or the straight line between readings within 15 min), cfs x 0.0283168 = m3/s; any hour without a valid USGS value uses that hour's NWM value and is flagged; if USGS cannot be read the inlet is NWM for all hours and the run metadata says so. Forecast hours are NWM short range unchanged. Provenance: live-case.json flowSources[].observed and inflowSource; manifest.json, road-forecast.json and local-road-forecast.json (top level and summary) carry inflowSource.
why: Round 1, 2026-11-01, reach 15876941 against USGS 09487000 (tools/sfincs/data/brawley-avra-west-v1/nwm-vs-usgs-09487000.json): the frozen case inflow after 14Z comes from the NWM short_range forecast issued at 13Z, which peaked at 1.70 m3/s (nwmFrozenCaseInflow, nwmForecastIssue13zMax). The NWM analysis_assim series, which live runs use for past hours when no gauge value exists, peaked at 46.8 m3/s at 23Z (nwmAnalysisFullWindow), against the observed peak of 49.27 m3/s (1740 cfs) at 21:30Z (observed15minInWindow). For past hours the gauge replaces a series that was about 1.5 h late and 5% low at the peak, not one that was 1.70 m3/s; the forecast hours stay NWM short_range and keep that issue's under-prediction.
